title: “Concert de casseroles” against recent COVID measures: second-evening street actions
location: Libreville (including PK7, Louis and other unnamed neighborhoods), Akanda, Owendo and Port-Gentil are reported; specific street clashes are described at PK7, Louis and other neighborhoods.
scope: Multiple localities are reported. The source does not establish national coordination or whether all locations were part of one organized event.
organizer: Unknown; the source says the action was initiated but does not name an organizer.
participants_original: The report says multiple residents of Libreville, Akanda, Owendo and Port-Gentil took part on the second evening. It gives no numerical attendance.
threshold_50_evidence: Not established. “Multiple residents” across locations has no numeric lower bound and cannot be aggregated across cities to meet a site-level threshold.

title.summary: Opened Gabon Media Time report describes the second evening of casserole protest action against recent government measures.

start_date.summary: Report dates the second evening to Thursday 18 February. The prior evening, 17 February, is inferred from that sequence; whether the first-night action included a qualifying public assembly is not established.

location.summary: Report says residents in Libreville, Akanda, Owendo and Port-Gentil participated; street confrontations are specified at PK7, Louis and other neighborhoods. No site-level count or complete site map is provided.

scope.summary: Several cities/communes are named, but this single account does not establish common organization, a national call, or episode boundaries across sites.

organizer.summary: No organizer is named in the read article section.

demands.summary: The report says the casserole action opposed recent government measures described as abusive; category coded as social restrictions.

participants.summary: The article uses qualitative wording about multiple residents and supplies no number.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No number, site-level lower bound, or count method is reported; threshold remains unresolved.

protester_violence.summary: The account mentions stones and alleged shop looting but does not clearly attribute all acts to the protest assembly rather than individuals; leave unknown.

state_response.summary: The account reports arrests and video of agents striking detained people with pots. It says shots were heard and people may have died without establishing who fired or confirming deaths; code arrests and beatings yes as reported, killings and shootings unknown.

end_date.summary: No end or physical close is stated. Later articles/search results do not establish this event’s end.

notes: The 17 February start is an explicit inference from the article’s description of Thursday 18 February as the second evening. Candidate remains pending because no >=50 site-level attendance is established. Reported attendance at multiple locations is not combined into one campaign crowd. Reported police actions and violence are retained as claims from this source, not independent confirmation.
open_questions: Did the first evening on 17 February include a qualifying public gathering, or only home-based noise?
Was a 50-person threshold met at any individual site?
Were the locations coordinated by one organizer or call?
Who fired shots, and were deaths confirmed by contemporaneous records?
What response occurred after the article’s 19 February publication time?
When did physical protest activity end?
